How Much Is Hulu Without Ads? Every Plan, Bundle, and Hidden Cost - Budget Seniors

# How Much Is Hulu Without Ads? Every Plan, Bundle, and Hidden Cost

 Budget Seniors, September 1, 2026 September 1, 2026 

$18.99/mo · No Annual Discount · Some Shows Still Run Ads · Project Gemini Merger Underway

Hulu without ads is $18.99 per month — but that’s only part of the picture. Some shows still play commercials on the “no ads” plan, no annual discount exists, and Disney is actively migrating the standalone Hulu app into Disney+. Here’s everything subscribers need to know before paying a dollar.

 Reviewed by Margaret L. Forsythe, Consumer Technology Analyst Streaming Industry Researcher · 14 Years Consumer Tech Coverage · Former Senior Editor, Cable & Telecom Review 

 $18.99 Hulu No Ads monthly price — standalone, monthly billing only, no annual option 

 Still Ads Some ABC and network-licensed shows still run brief pre-roll ads — even on the No Ads plan 

📋 Key Takeaways — The Real Answers Before You Subscribe

These are the questions Hulu does not answer prominently on its own pricing page. The answers are short and direct — scroll down for the longer explanations of each.

1 How much is Hulu without ads per month, and is there an annual discount?

Hulu (No Ads) costs $18.99 per month. There is no annual billing option — only monthly. The with-ads plan offers an annual rate of $119.99 per year (roughly $10 per month), saving about $24 compared to twelve monthly payments. That annual discount does not exist for the No Ads tier. Over a full year, the No Ads plan costs $227.88 — $108 more per year than the annual with-ads option. Whether that gap is worth it depends entirely on how much you watch and how much commercial breaks frustrate you.

2 Does “No Ads” mean zero commercials on every show?

No — not on every show. A small set of programs, primarily current ABC network series (Grey’s Anatomy, Abbott Elementary, Station 19, and others), still carry brief 15–30 second non-skippable ads at the start or end of episodes. This happens because Hulu’s licensing agreements with certain broadcast networks require it as a condition of streaming rights. The ads don’t interrupt episodes mid-scene, but they are there. Hulu discloses this in its plan description with language noting “limited commercial interruptions” on select titles. Hulu Originals, most FX content, and the movie library are genuinely ad-free. Heavy watchers of ABC primetime will encounter these ads regularly.

3 Is the No Ads plan worth $7 more per month than the with-ads plan?

For anyone watching ten or more hours of Hulu per week, the math usually works out — Hulu’s ad load runs roughly four to six minutes per hour on the with-ads tier, so a heavy binge session accumulates real commercial time. For casual viewers watching two or three episodes a week, the with-ads plan is difficult to justify upgrading from. The smartest move: start with the with-ads plan, watch it for one billing cycle, and decide from personal experience rather than assumption. Hulu allows upgrades at any time from your account settings with no penalty and no resubscription required.

4 What is the cheapest way to get Hulu without ads?

The Disney Bundle Duo Premium — Hulu (No Ads) plus Disney+ (No Ads) — costs $19.99 per month, just one dollar more than standalone Hulu No Ads at $18.99. That extra dollar adds the entire ad-free Disney+ library: every Marvel and Star Wars title, Pixar, National Geographic, and Disney Originals. Standalone Disney+ (No Ads) costs $13.99 on its own, so the bundle delivers roughly $12 in monthly savings compared to subscribing to both services separately. For most people, the Duo Premium is simply the better buy.

5 Does Hulu No Ads include live TV?

No. The $18.99 plan is on-demand streaming only — no live channels, no local news, no sports broadcasts. Hulu + Live TV (No Ads) costs $99.99 per month and adds 95+ live channels along with Disney+ (No Ads) and ESPN Select. C

Expected Dec 2026

Disney is winding down the standalone Hulu app and migrating its content into Disney+ under a plan called 'Project Gemini,' targeted for the end of 2026. The app would be decommissioned once users transition, though Disney says there are 'no current plans to sunset' it.

### How much is Hulu per month in 2026?

Hulu costs $12.49 to $21.49 per month as of October 2026, depending on the plan: With Ads at $12.49 and No Ads at $21.49.

### How much is Hulu per year?

At $21.49/month, Hulu (No Ads) costs $257.88 per year when paying monthly. The With Ads plan works out to $149.88 per year. This site tracks standard monthly rates, so discounted annual plans, where offered, are not included.

### How much has Hulu gone up over time?

### Is this the standalone Hulu price or the Disney+ bundle?

### What is the difference between Hulu and Hulu + Live TV?

Hulu costs $12.49 a month with ads and $21.49 a month without ads in the US after Disney's latest price rise. New subscribers pay that now; existing members move on their first bill on or after October 21, 2026. Hulu + Live TV is $99.99 a month with ads.

Here is the twist that most price guides miss: the Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads costs $12.99, just 50 cents more than Hulu on its own, and the ad-free bundle is $21.99, also 50 cents more than ad-free Hulu. For almost everyone, buying Hulu by itself no longer makes sense. This guide covers every plan, what you actually get, the bundles, student and carrier deals, price history and who should pay for what.

Prices checked October 2, 2026

Prices from Disney's September 23, 2026 US price announcement: Hulu with ads $12.49 (was $11.99), Hulu Premium (no ads) $21.49 (was $18.99), Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads $12.99 (unchanged), bundle Premium $21.99 (was $19.99), Hulu + Live TV $99.99 with ads or $109.99 without (both up $10). Hulu's US plan page was geo-blocked from our test location, so we confirmed these against multiple reports of Disney's announcement.

The short answer

- Hulu with ads: $12.49 a month. The bundle with Disney+ is $12.99. Buy the bundle.
- Hulu Premium (no ads): $21.49. The ad-free Disney+ and Hulu bundle is $21.99. Again, buy the bundle.
- Students: the Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads is $6.49; the older $1.99 Hulu-only student plan may not be open to new signups.
- Hulu + Live TV: $99.99 with ads, and it already includes Disney+ and ESPN.
- Hulu has raised prices every October since 2021. Plan on another rise in late 2027.

### The fine print

- "No ads" is not quite no ads. A handful of shows on Hulu Premium still play short ads before and after episodes because of licensing deals. Hulu lists them with a "no ads" exception. It is a few titles, not a lot, but it surprises people.
- No downloads on the ad plan. Offline viewing is Premium-only.
- Two screens. Families with three or four TVs need the Unlimited Screens add-on, which is only available with Hulu + Live TV.
- The Hulu app is moving into Disney+. During 2026 Disney is folding Hulu content into the Disney+ app. Standalone Hulu plans are still sold, but more and more of the experience lives in Disney+, which is another reason the bundle makes sense.
- Price rises apply to existing members after a 30-day notice. There is no grandfathering.

Hulu Subscription Cost Per Month (2026) - Budget Seniors

# Hulu Subscription Cost Per Month (2026)

 Budget Seniors, September 27, 2026 September 27, 2026 

Disney raised Hulu’s prices again in late September. The ad-free plan jumped $2.50 to $21.49 a month, the basic plan went up 50 cents, and Hulu + Live TV crossed the $100 line for the no-ads version. What didn’t go up is more interesting: the Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads stayed at $12.99. That’s just 50 cents more than Hulu by itself. This guide walks through what you’ll actually pay, when the new price hits an existing account, and which plan fits the way you really watch.

 The short answer Hulu alone now costs $12.49/month with ads or $21.49 without. Unless you truly never watch Disney+, the Disney+ and Hulu bundle is the better buy at $12.99 with ads or $21.99 without, just 50 cents over Hulu alone. Hulu + Live TV is now $99.99 ($109.99 with ad-free on-demand). That’s worth it mainly if you watch live local news or sports most days. If you’re already subscribed, the new rate lands on your bill on or after October 21, depending on your billing date. 

 Reviewed By Gregory Tam — Streaming & Cord-Cutting Cost Analyst 11 Years Tracking Streaming Prices, Bundles & Live TV Services · Contributor, SatelliteInternetGuide.com 

$12.49 Hulu with ads, standalone (up 50¢)

$21.49 Hulu Premium, no ads (up $2.50)

$12.99 Disney+ & Hulu bundle with ads (unchanged)

$99.99 Hulu + Live TV (up $10)

## Key Answers People Want First

These cover the questions that come up the moment a price-increase email lands in the inbox.

1 When will my bill actually go up?

New subscribers started paying the higher prices on September 23. If you already subscribe, the increase applies on or after October 21, on your first billing date after that. Annual subscribers are included in this round too, at their next renewal. Disney emails existing customers about the change. That email is the most reliable record of what your new rate will be.

2 Why would anyone pay for Hulu alone now?

For most people, there’s little reason to. Hulu with ads is $12.49, and the Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads is $12.99. The ad-free versions follow the same pattern: $21.49 for Hulu alone, $21.99 for both. For 50 cents a month you get the full Disney+ library too: Pixar, Marvel, Star Wars, and National Geographic. Grandchildren tend to find that library first when they visit. Switching from standalone Hulu to the bundle is done under your account’s plan settings.

3 Does “No Ads” really mean no ads?

Mostly, not entirely. Hulu’s own terms say a small number of shows still play a brief ad before and after an episode, even on Premium. That’s because of the licensing deals behind those shows. The long mid-episode breaks disappear. If you pay for Premium and get mid-episode ads on a Hulu Original, that’s a glitch worth reporting to Hulu support. Live channels on Hulu + Live TV always carry regular commercials, like cable.

4 What happened to the $1.99 student deal?

New students can no longer sign up for $1.99 standalone Hulu through Hulu’s student page. The current offer is the Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads for $6.49/month, half the regular $12.99. It lasts as long as you’re verified as a student at an accredited U.S. college or trade school. Verification runs through SheerID and must be renewed every year. It only works when you pay Disney or Hulu directly, not through an app store or a cable company.

5 Is the Hulu app going away?

The separate Hulu app is being phased out, but your Hulu subscription isn’t. Disney has already moved Hulu’s full catalog into the Disney+ app. The Hulu app stopped working on the Nintendo Switch in February. CEO Bob Iger has said he expects the full one-app setup to arrive by the end of the calendar year. Disney says you’ll still be able to buy Hulu on its own. # Hulu Plans Compared: Price of Every Plan, Bundle and Add-on, October 2026

Hulu is $12.49 with ads or $124.99 a year, Premium $21.49, Disney+ bundles from $12.99, Live TV from $99.99 and Live TV Only $98.99. Every plan and add-on price, listed.

Published Oct 11, 2026 Checked against official sources · last verified Oct 11, 2026 · how we verify

Hulu sells one streaming library at eleven different prices, depending on what you bundle with it. As of October 10, 2026, Hulu’s own plans and prices page lists Hulu (With Ads) at $12.49 a month or $124.99 a year, Hulu Premium at $21.49, the Disney+, Hulu Bundle at $12.99 or $21.99, the HBO Max bundles at $21.99 or $34.99, Hulu + Live TV from $99.99, and a Live TV Only plan at $98.99 that drops the Hulu library altogether. These are the prices for new subscriptions since September 23, 2026; the page says anyone who signed up earlier sees the new price “in your billing cycle on or after October 21, 2026.” This guide puts every plan and add-on price on one page, does the arithmetic Hulu’s page leaves out, and flags the one row that moved since our last read. If you are leaving instead, the steps and the bundle catch are in our Hulu cancellation guide.

## The quick answer

- Hulu (With Ads): $12.49 a month, or $124.99 a year ($10.42 a month by our math)
- Hulu Premium (No Ads): $21.49 a month, with downloads and Watch Party, no annual option listed
- Disney+, Hulu Bundle: $12.99 with ads, $21.99 with no ads on both, 50 cents over Hulu alone
- Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Select Bundle: $21.99 with ads, $32.99 Premium
- Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited Bundle: $35.99, or $44.99 Premium
- Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max Bundle: $21.99 with ads, $34.99 with no ads
- Hulu + Live TV: $99.99 with Disney+ and ESPN Select, $109.99 with Hulu and Disney+ ad-free, $98.99 for Live TV Only
- New prices: for new subscribers from September 23, 2026; existing subscribers from their billing cycle on or after October 21, 2026

# How Much Does Hulu Cost? Every Plan Compared

Updated July 30, 2026 · 4 min read

## Short answer

Hulu with ads is 11.99 dollars a month and the ad-free plan is 18.99. The Disney+, Hulu and ESPN Select ad-supported bundle at 19.99 costs less than buying Disney+ and Hulu separately. Hulu is US only; elsewhere its content sits inside Disney+ under the Hulu hub.

## Key takeaways

- Hulu with ads is $11.99 a month, and Hulu with no ads is $18.99 a month.
- The Disney+, Hulu and ESPN Select ad-supported bundle is $19.99, which is cheaper than Disney+ and Hulu bought separately.
- Hulu + Live TV starts at $89.99 and already includes Disney+ and ESPN Select.
- Hulu is a US service. In the UK and Canada, Hulu content sits inside Disney+ under the Hulu hub rather than as a separate subscription.

Hulu has more pricing paths than almost any other streaming service, and the standalone plan is rarely the cheapest way in. Here is every 2026 option side by side.

## Hulu on-demand plans

The two core plans have not changed shape, only price.

| Plan | Monthly | Annual | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hulu (With Ads) | $11.99 | $119.99 | Full on-demand catalogue, ads |
| Hulu (No Ads) | $18.99 | Not offered | Same catalogue, ads removed on most titles |

Two details matter. The annual ad-supported plan works out around $10 a month, which is a genuine saving of roughly $24 a year if you are certain you will keep it for 12 months. And "No Ads" is not absolutely ad-free: a small number of titles still carry pre-roll or post-roll ads because of licensing terms.

## Hulu + Live TV

This is a different product wearing the same name. Hulu + Live TV starts at $89.99 a month for the ad-supported version and includes 95 or more live channels, unlimited DVR, and Disney+ and ESPN Select at no extra charge.

At that price it competes with cable, not with streaming apps. It only makes sense if you specifically want live sports and news channels. If you are here because you want to watch on-demand shows, the $11.99 plan is the product you want.

One thing to watch: Disney has proposed moving Hulu's live TV business into a joint venture with Fubo, which means live TV subscribers may be migrated to a Fubo-operated service. If you are signing up for live TV specifically, that is worth knowing before you commit to anything annual.

## The bundles, which is where the value is

If you want Hulu and anything else Disney owns, the bundle is not a marketing trick, it is simply cheaper.

| Bundle | Monthly | Includes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Select (ad-supported) | $19.99 | All three with ads |
| Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Select Premium | $29.99 | All three ad-free |
| Hulu + Live TV (ad-supported) | $89.99 | Live TV plus Disney+ and ESPN Select |

The ad-supported bundle at $19.99 is the standout. Buying Disney+ with ads and Hulu with ads on separate bills costs more than $19.99, so the bundle gives you ESPN Select for less than nothing. If you currently pay two separate Disney and Hulu bills, switching is free money.

The Premium bundle at $29.99 makes ad-free Hulu look expensive on its own: $18.99 for Hulu ad-free alone against $29.99 for three services ad-free. If ad-free matters to you and you watch any Disney+ at all, the bundle wins.

## Discounts worth checking

- Students. Eligible college students get Hulu with ads for $1.99 a month with verification. That is the cheapest legitimate Hulu in existence and it renews for as long as you stay verified.
- Military. Active-duty and veteran US military members get 25 percent off the ad-supported plan.
- Mobile and internet plans. Hulu is periodically included with certain phone and broadband plans. Check what your carrier already gives you before paying separately, because people routinely pay for a service their plan already covers.
